facts.statement: The species Iteravis huchzermeyeri was named to honor Dr. Fritz Huchzermeyer, an archosaur paleontologist who died just before the genus was described.
facts.quote: Iteravis huchzermeyeri, named in honor of the archosaur palaeontologist Dr. Fritz Huchzermeyer, who died shortly before Iteravis was described.

facts.statement: Iteravis is an extinct ornithuromorph bird found in the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: Iteravis () is an extinct genus of ornithuromorph bird known from the Early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation of what is today the Liaoning Province of China.

facts.statement: Scientists debate whether Iteravis is a synonym of Gansus zheni or a distinct genus closely related to Gansus within the family Gansuidae.
facts.quote: The relationships between Iteravis and species of Gansus have been debated, with some researchers arguing for a synonymy between the former and G. zheni, and others recovering a closer relationship between the two genera within the family Gansuidae.

facts.statement: In 2018, Wang and colleagues identified three new specimens from the Sihedang locality that, along with existing fossils, represent the only known ornithurines from that site.
facts.quote: In 2018, Wang and colleagues described three new specimens similar to Iteravis huchzermeyeri and Gansus zheni, together comprising the only ornithurines described from the Sihedang locality of the Jiufotang Formation.

facts.statement: In 2021, Ju and colleagues concluded that Iteravis huchzermeyeri and Gansus zheni are the same species based on a detailed comparison.
facts.quote: Shortly thereafter, Ju and colleagues (2021) independently published a more detailed comparison of I. huchzermeyeri and G. zheni. Similar to Wang et al. (2018), these authors concluded that the two species are synonymous.

facts.statement: O'Connor and colleagues (2021) treated Iteravis huchzermeyeri and Gansus zheni as distinct species despite observing small differences of uncertain taxonomic significance.
facts.quote: O'Connor and colleagues (2021) expressed that there are small differences observed between I. huchzermeyeri and G. zheni of "uncertain taxonomic significance". As such, they treated the two species as distinct, pending more thorough research.

facts.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses by Wang et al. (2025) and Huang et al. (2026) recovered Iteravis as the sister taxon to Gansus yumenensis.
facts.quote: Wang et al., 2025 (describing Shuilingornis angelai) and Huang et al., 2026 (describing Kunpengornis anhuimusei), both using phylogenetic matrices developed by Andrea Cau, recovered Iteravis as the sister taxon to Gansus yumenensis.

facts.statement: Iteravis consumed larger food particles than Archaeorhynchus, though the precise details of its diet are still unknown.
facts.quote: Iteravis ate larger particles of food than Archaeorhynchus, although the exact details of its diet remain enigmatic.

facts.statement: Iteravis lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous, between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)
